A well-known Chinese leaker with a solid track record has recently published what are claimed to be circuit schematics for the next-generation iPhone 18 Pro series.

From the images, it can be seen that the new A20 Pro chip may feature seven GPU cores — one more than the previous generation — along with a faster memory interface…

These images were posted by Weibo user「定焦數碼」(Fixed Focus Digital), and what they show is not the A20 Pro chip itself, but rather a diagram indicating where the chip would be soldered onto the underlying circuit board. From this, the leaker inferred the performance and architecture of the new chip and drew two main conclusions believed to be likely areas of improvement.

First, the images show that the CPU core configuration remains the same as last year — a total of six cores, including two high-performance cores and four efficiency cores. However, the efficiency cores appear to be equipped with larger cache memory.

Based solely on the limited information provided by the soldering pad location diagram, it is difficult to determine the GPU core count — six, seven, or even eight are all possible options. However, the leaker ultimately judged that seven cores is the most likely.

「定焦數碼」previously also pointed out that the A20 Pro chip will deliver an 18% performance improvement over the previous generation, along with a 30% improvement in power efficiency.

9to5Mac's take

Although this Weibo account does have a certain degree of credibility, this method of indirect inference carries considerable limitations. Even if its conclusions seem reasonable, readers should not treat them as fact — at most, they should be regarded as well-reasoned speculation.
